activities.name: Travelling in the harmattan
activities.note: nothing closes; the harmattan blows during the dry season — the trade-off is the dust

windows.reason: the months the harmattan blows most: its Saharan dust can severely limit visibility for days at a time, and humidity can drop below 15%
the edges of the harmattan season, which runs from the end of November to the middle of March

activities.name: Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary
activities.note: far fewer birds, and in the rains the sanctuary shuts for about three months because moving about becomes impossible

windows.reason: the migration peak, with close to 400 bird species in the park
either side of the peak: the migration gets going in December and thins after mid-February
the rains: the park is officially closed, though a visit may be arranged with an eco-guard; many roads are impassable and there are far fewer birds

activities.name: Niokolo-Koba National Park
activities.note: in the rains (late June to late October) the animals disperse and the tracks need 4WD more than ever

windows.reason: dry season: the best game viewing, from the end of October to the end of June, when most tours run
held every May: five days of jazz and world music centred on Saint-Louis's Place Baya; dates are set each year
